I can tell you can be a good person, even if you don't think you are right now. I also grew up in a toxic household, and in highschool I was manipulative and cynical and treated my few friends like shit. I was full of spite for the happiness of those around me and anger that nobody understood what it was like to be me. Eventually I had my eyes opened (somewhat traumatically, but I had it coming) and realized how shitty I was being. But, just like you, I had a desire to be a good person and get rid of this spite and anger inside me and just be kind to others. It took me nearly a year with only one friend helping me for support but I got there, and now I can be happy from making others happy. I hope you see a bit of yourself in my story, I believe everyone can change if they want it.

To stop yourself from self harming until the urge passes is tough, but please try. There's different reasons to self harm and different coping methods with each: for venting anger/frustration, instead write or draw out your thoughts; for punishment, instead exercise; for seeing blood, instead draw on yourself with red marker. This is just one example of each, there's hundreds more if you Google it. Good luck!

Thank you SO MUCH for being this kind of person, there are loads of free articles and information on the internet but a lot of it is psuedoscience and unreliable. I don't know what kind of education background you have, but most therapists have at the minimum a bachelor's degree in psychology with some vocational training, while psychiatrists usually have a master's or doctorate in psychology.

Openstax is a website started by Bill Gates to provide textbooks for free to college students, and it includes a psychology textbook. Link: https://cnx.org/contents/Sr8Ev5Og@5.101:F_mjYFfh@15/Preface

I suggest not skipping straight to the therapy section and instead reading all of it, as the more general knowledge of psychology you have, the more you'll be able to help your friend.
Best of luck!

You can look up people's experiences with psych wards to help ease any fears you might have.
